slides.eyebrow: I rented 10+ years. Paid $150K+ in rent.
slides.sub: Step one out of renting is preapproval, and here are the 3 piles of paperwork lenders ask for.

slides.title: Pile 1: your income
items: Pay stubs from the last 2 months
Tax returns for 2 years (often needed if you're self-employed or earn commission or rental income)

slides.title: Pile 2: your money
items: A gift letter if you're using gift money

slides.title: Pile 3: who you are
items: Employers and home addresses for the past 2 years
Proof of rent payments or your lease

slides.title: The lender checks your credit
slides.body: Lenders look at your income, assets, debts and credit. A preapproval letter usually expires in 30 to 60 days. Ask your lender for their exact list. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.

caption:
If I had to start over, I'd stop renting a lot sooner. I rented for over 10 years and paid over $150K in rent.

The first step out of renting is preapproval, and it starts with 3 piles of paperwork: your income (pay stubs, W-2s, tax returns), your money (account statements and a gift letter if you're using gift money), and who you are (photo ID, 2 years of job and address history, proof of rent). A preapproval letter usually expires in 30 to 60 days.

Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
